_meta.description: Validation data collected from independent sources (textbooks, solved examples in the style of Mattingly and Cohen-Rogers). Each record: source, inputs, reference (book) results, and the assumptions made when translating the case to GCAM. The tests read this file, run the corresponding component or the full cycle, and compare.
_meta.wired: Records with wired=true are run automatically. Records with wired=false are documented for later and not yet validated automatically.

cases.source: Mattingly, Aircraft Engine Design: AAF reference point (ONX output)
cases.description: Formula-level check of the MIL-E-5008B supersonic inlet recovery (without running the engine).
cases.notes: Same MIL-E-5008B formula as mil_inlet_recovery() (from Mattingly); an exact match is expected.

cases.source: Mattingly, Aircraft Engine Design: AAF test point (M0=1.8 / 40 kft)
cases.description: MIL-E-5008B check at a second, higher Mach flight point of the same engine.
cases.notes: Same engine (constant pi_d_max), different M0: checks the M0 dependence at a second point.

cases.source: Cohen-Rogers, Gas Turbine Theory, Example 2.1 (single shaft with heat exchanger; only the compressor step is used)
cases.description: Low pressure ratio compressor with isentropic efficiency (eta_c given directly).
cases.notes: The book uses cpa = 1.005 kJ/kgK; GCAM uses R = 287.05 and gamma_c = 1.4 -> cpc = 1004.175 J/kgK (0.08 % difference). Tt3 does not depend on cp (only on pressure ratio and efficiency), so a close match is expected.

cases.source: Cohen-Rogers, Gas Turbine Theory, Example 2.2 (simple cycle with free power turbine; gas generator compressor)
cases.description: Medium pressure ratio compressor with isentropic efficiency, plus combustor pressure loss.
cases.notes: pi_b = 0.94, the book's '6 % compressor delivery pressure loss' (Pt3_after_burner_loss = Pt3_comp_exit * 0.94 = 12.0 * 0.94 = 11.28 bar).

cases.source: Cohen-Rogers, Gas Turbine Theory, Example 2.3 (high pressure ratio reheat cycle; gas generator compressor)
cases.description: High pressure ratio compressor with polytropic efficiency: tests the use_polytropic=true branch.
cases.notes: Polytropic branch: compressor_tau_from_polytropic() is the same as the book's (n-1)/n = (1/e_c)(gamma-1)/gamma.

cases.source: Cohen-Rogers, Gas Turbine Theory, Example 2.2 (gas generator turbine; pressure ratio from the work balance)
cases.description: The turbine pressure ratio is solved backwards so that the turbine just drives the compressor: the same technique as GCAM's isentropic turbine branch.
cases.notes: Called with f = 0: the book neglects the (1+f) factor in the turbine work balance (a known textbook simplification, confirmed in the Example 3.1 check). GCAM's default mode (f included) gives about 0.5 % higher Tt5; this is physically more accurate, not an error. Wc_Jkg = 348130 from the book's Tt3-Tt2 = 346.3 K with cpc = 1004.175 (rounding within tolerance).

cases.source: Mattingly, Elements of Gas Turbine Propulsion, Chapter 7 (parametric cycle with losses), Example 7-1
cases.description: Turbojet combustor fuel/air ratio from the closed-form energy balance Eq. 7-10: f = (cpt*Tt4 - cpc*Tt3) / (eta_b*hPR - cpt*Tt4). This is exactly GCAM's ideal (CPG, constant cpc/cph) combustor formula.
cases.notes: Tt3_K is derived from the book's M0 = 2, T0 = 216.7 K, tau_r = 1.8, tau_c = 2.0771 (pi_c = 10, e_c = 0.9): Tt3 = tau_r*tau_c*T0 = 810.19 K. Pt3_bar is arbitrary: the f calculation does not use it, so only f is checked. With the book's own cpc = 1.004 and cpt = 1.239 kJ/(kg K) the formula gives f = 0.035674 (0.01 % from the book's 0.03567): the formula is identical. The measured difference (0.6 %, GCAM = 0.0359) comes from GCAM deriving cp from a single R = 287.05 and gamma (cph = 1243.9 vs the book's 1239, which uses separate Rc/Rt). Tolerance set to 0.7 %.

cases.source: Cohen-Rogers, Gas Turbine Theory, Example 3.1 (simple turbojet, choked convergent nozzle, design point)
cases.description: Choked convergent nozzle: P9 > Pamb, the pressure thrust term is active.
cases.notes: Fixed: the choked branch used to compute P9 isentropically (eta_n not used). With nozzle_critical_pr_with_loss() (Cohen-Rogers Eq. 3.14) P9 = Pt9/crit_PR and the choking threshold now include eta_n. The difference dropped from 3.3 % to 0.28 % (GCAM 0.6691 bar, book 0.671 bar). crit_PR: GCAM 1.9189 vs book 1.914 (rounding).

cases.source: Cohen-Rogers, Gas Turbine Theory, Example 3.2 (two-spool turbofan, static), step 4: cold (fan) nozzle
cases.description: Unchoked nozzle (full expansion, P9 = Pamb): tests the physical branch, which is the same for 'conv' and 'cd' when unchoked.
cases.notes: The fan stream is air (gamma = 1.4), not hot products. Passing gamma_h = 1.4 isolates cold-stream physics at component level (no separate cold nozzle in GCAM's turbojet model). PR = 1.65 is far from the critical ratio (~1.965), so assert_choked = true is safe.

cases.source: Cohen-Rogers, Gas Turbine Theory, Example 3.2 (two-spool turbofan, static), step 8: hot (core) nozzle
cases.notes: Fixed: a borderline case (PR = 1.878). The purely isentropic critical ratio (1.852) used to classify it as choked, while the book's critical ratio including eta_j (1.914) says unchoked. With nozzle_critical_pr_with_loss() GCAM's critical ratio is 1.9189 > 1.878, so it is now unchoked as in the book.

cases.source: Cohen-Rogers, Gas Turbine Theory, Example 3.1 (simple turbojet design point)
cases.description: Full cycle: inlet -> compressor -> combustor -> turbine -> choked convergent nozzle. The most complete test.
cases.notes: pi_d_max = 0.9729 is back-calculated so that the MIL-E-5008B model matches the book's inlet loss model (eta_i = 0.93). FHV is not given in the book; standard kerosene 43.1 MJ/kg is assumed. The whole Tt5/Pt5/T9 difference comes from the book neglecting (1+f) in the turbine work balance (GCAM is more accurate). The P9/F_spec difference was reduced by the eta_n critical pressure fix: P9 5.30 % -> 1.65 %, F_spec 4.99 % -> 3.99 %; the rest comes from Tt5/Pt5, not from the nozzle.

deferred_cases_summary: Mattingly AAF mixed-flow afterburning turbofan full-cycle examples (Sample Printout A/B/C): imperial units and a two-spool bypass architecture that does not map directly to GCAM's simplified turbofan model.

Combustion chemistry / stoichiometry examples (atom balance, equivalence ratio phi): no independent atom-balance example found to test the real_gas product mixture assumption (C12H23, phi_eq = f/FST).

Cohen-Rogers Examples 2.1/2.2/2.3 combustor f values were tried and left out on purpose: the book reads f from temperature-rise charts, GCAM uses the FHV energy balance. Reproducing Example 2.2's f = 0.0204 would need FHV = 46.82 MJ/kg, which is unrealistic. Covered instead by Mattingly Example 7-1 ('combustor_eogtp_real_ex71').
GasTurb compressor map scaling examples: they depend on GasTurb's internal generic map data, which is not available.
Mattingly Table 5.2 (single-stage impulse turbine off-design, blade speed sweep): a blade/aerodynamic level calculation, not comparable with GCAM's thermodynamic cycle model.
